clue.text: Resist having to get up

parts.note: having means with, as in a house with a garden
to get up is to stand

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to rise to their feet as an act of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand an attack is to resist it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: River in which we serve

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A waiter points out a river where we serve customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'we serve' with no break.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weser is a German river flowing to the North Sea.

clue.text: Can class provide old photograph?

parts.note: a can is a tin
a class or kind is a type

explanation.surface: A question whether a tin-can category could give us a vintage snapshot.
explanation.definitionFit: A tintype is an early photograph printed on a thin iron plate.

clue.text: Killed in turn

definitions.meaning: past tense of slay, meaning put to death
as a verb it means swing round or veer sharply

explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: past tense of slay, and a verb for swinging round or veering.

clue.text: Books and articles about pop stars

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the articles wrap around the books

parts.note: A is the indefinite article, taken twice
B is an abbreviation for book, so books is BB

explanation.surface: A library of books and essays written on famous pop musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: Two A's go on either side of BB.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA were a Swedish group, among the best-known pop stars of the 1970s.

clue.text: Note shared accommodation

definitions.meaning: a musical sign lowering a note by two semitones, or the note so written
a flat that two people share, read playfully

explanation.definitionFit: In music a double flat is a note lowered two semitones; jokingly, a flat for two.

clue.text: Salts' place — in the deep, somewhere

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is concealed in the following words

explanation.surface: A guess at where salts come from: somewhere in the ocean depths.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle 'deep, somewhere'. Epsom salts are named after Epsom, a town in Surrey, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts take their name from the Surrey spa town where the mineral water was found.

clue.text: Curse of senior manager on dole

parts.note: exec is short for executive, a senior manager
to dole out is to ration, and a ration is a dole or allotted share

explanation.surface: A boss laid off and on the dole swears bitterly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the dole after the manager in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An execration is a curse or loud denunciation, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Sequin found in corner shop previously empty

indicators.note: previously says this piece comes before the next one
an empty word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a corner is an angle

explanation.surface: A sequin turns up in the corner of a shop that had been empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' keeps only the outside letters of shop, and 'previously' sets them before the corner; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A spangle is a small shiny ornament sewn on clothes, the same thing as a sequin.

clue.text: Holding first of talks, was go-between considered?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to act as a go-between is to mediate

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A negotiator in the opening talks wonders whether their mediation was well thought out.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the first letter of talks, goes inside MEDIATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have meditated on something is to have considered it carefully.

clue.text: Assured novel, but wilder movie

indicators.note: wilder means more unruly, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A confident book, but the director Billy Wilder made a film instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like the definition but is fodder; 'wilder' rearranges ASSURED NOVEL BUT. Billy Wilder directed the film, a neat surface touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunset Boulevard is the 1950 Hollywood film directed by Billy Wilder.

clue.text: Boost sound or light

indicators.note: sound tells us to take how the word is said, not spelt

parts.note: to boost is to raise

explanation.surface: A choice between turning up the volume or the brightness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a noun in the surface (sound or light) but is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Light travels as rays, so rays of the sun stand for light.

clue.text: One-sided acquiescence?

parts.note: an agreeing phrase read literally as being entirely on one side, the side opposite left

explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes casually is agreeing, and read word by word it is wholly right-hand.

clue.text: He fools around with power, say, for online device

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so fools wraps the word he

parts.note: clots are fools
taken as written
P is the abbreviation for power in physics
say means for example, abbreviated EG

explanation.surface: A man messes about with electricity, perhaps, to build an internet gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'online' means on a washing line, not on the internet.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes peg is a gadget that holds washing on the line.

clue.text: Challenged Catholic leader on "Father Ted" carries on

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word before
carries means bears within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Catholic leader takes on the TV sitcom Father Ted, which keeps going regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carries' puts ON inside FRTED to make FRONTED, after C and ON. Father Ted is a British sitcom about Irish priests.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confronted is to be challenged face to face.

clue.text: Scarper when dice game's unsatisfactory

parts.note: beetle is a party game where players roll a die to draw a beetle
off means not up to standard, as in an off day

explanation.surface: Someone flees when a game at the table goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Beetle is a British party dice game; 'beetle off' is British slang for hurry away.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle off is informal British for to scurry away, which is to scarper.

clue.text: Skinny people plan to mingle with obese

indicators.note: mingle means mix together, so the two words' letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Thin people intend to socialise with heavy ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanpoles is informal for tall, very thin people, like the poles for bean plants.

clue.text: Article's first and last — first and last taking articles?

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: first and last picks the opening and closing letters of the next phrase

explanation.surface: A puzzle about first and last letters that ends by asking about stealing things.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'first and last' starts with F and ends with T. 'articles' in the definition means items or objects, not grammar words.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is stealing, which is taking other people's things or items.

clue.text: A prodigious sailor's cry

parts.note: prodigious means enormous, vast

explanation.surface: A huge seaman bellowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the nautical call meaning stop or hold, used by sailors.

clue.text: Country song about American getting back from Detroit

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the song wraps the rest

parts.note: an aria is a solo song in opera

indicators.note: back from picks the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A country-and-western song about an American coming home from Detroit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country song' reads as one musical genre, but 'Country' is the definition and the song is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Austria is a country in central Europe.

clue.text: Rococo for a grand painter

indicators.note: rococo means highly ornate and fussy, so these letters are rearranged extravagantly

explanation.surface: Elaborate decoration chosen for a splendid painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Fragonard was a French painter of the rococo style, so the indicator fits the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Honore Fragonard was an eighteenth-century French artist.

clue.text: "The Entertainer" (with Archie Rice), initially based on a book by McCourt and Lawrence

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece based on another sits above it
initially picks the opening letters of the words before it

parts.note: 'Tis is Frank McCourt's memoir, sequel to Angela's Ashes
T. E. Lawrence, known as Lawrence of Arabia, gives his initials TE

explanation.surface: John Osborne's play The Entertainer, with its hero Archie Rice, said to derive from books by two authors.
explanation.walkthrough: Archie Rice is the music-hall performer in John Osborne's play The Entertainer; in this down clue 'based on' stacks his initials above the books.
explanation.definitionFit: An artiste is a professional performer such as a music-hall singer or dancer.

clue.text: Dumbbell brought into gym before fellow proceeded

indicators.note: before says this piece comes ahead of the next
brought into means put inside the following word

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym lessons
a dumbbell is a fool, an ass
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A weight carried into the gym before a man moved on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumbbell' suggests a weight, which fits the gym, but here it means a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To have passed on is to have gone ahead or proceeded, as on to the next item.

clue.text: Amaze head of school with union backing

indicators.note: head of picks the first letter of the following word
backing means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A headteacher astonishes everyone by getting the union's support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like support but turns NUT into TUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to astonish or amaze them.

clue.text: Contradictory answers given by poet

definitions.meaning: a negative reply followed by a positive one
Alfred ..., English poet who wrote The Highwayman

explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' is only a link between the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Two opposing replies side by side, and the surname of the poet Alfred.

clue.text: Dingy fish crossing river

indicators.note: crossing means lying across, so the fish goes either side of the river

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish
R is the abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A dull-coloured fish swims across a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and dreary, a synonym of dingy.

clue.text: Musical grunts?

parts.note: grunt is US slang for an infantryman, also called a GI
the second soldier, again a GI

explanation.surface: A question whether animal noises form a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grunts' suggests noises, but it is US slang for foot soldiers. Gigi is the Lerner and Loewe musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Gigi is a stage and film musical by Lerner and Loewe.

clue.text: Novel peer, mostly weird

indicators.note: novel means new and fresh, so these letters take a new order

explanation.surface: A fictional nobleman who is rather eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel peer' reads as the definition, but 'Novel' rearranges PEER MOSTLY WEIRD, and the whole clue describes Dorothy L. Sayers' detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers' aristocratic sleuth is a nobleman in novels, whimsical in manner.

clue.text: Refuse to accept name, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: slag is waste or refuse from smelting

explanation.surface: Declining to agree to a name, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like a verb (decline) but is a noun, waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang is informal vocabulary, a particular way of talking.

clue.text: Joyce's work is to name ships

parts.note: to dub is to give a name to
liners are large passenger ships

explanation.surface: James Joyce's task is christening vessels.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubliners is James Joyce's 1914 short-story collection.
